claims.text: A faster thermal ramp during precursor reduction reduces the time available for atomic mobility.
Limited atomic mobility during rapid processing kinetically traps the metal atoms.
Kinetic trapping preserves a disordered and compositionally uniform alloy state before diffusion can induce phase separation or elemental segregation.
A faster thermal ramp produces a more homogeneous noble metal high-entropy alloy nanoparticle structure.
A faster thermal ramp produces nanoparticles with greater surface-area exposure.
Slower thermal ramps provide sufficient time for atomic diffusion.
The additional diffusion available under slower ramps can cause phase separation.
The additional diffusion available under slower ramps can cause elemental segregation.
Slower ramps can produce uncontrolled or otherwise undesired nanoparticle morphologies.
An intermediate thermal ramp yields partially homogeneous but nonoptimized nanoparticle structures.
The proposed mechanism applies specifically to rapidly processed noble metal systems containing more than five elements.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to binary or simpler alloy systems.
The proposed mechanism may not apply when the synthesis method fundamentally changes precursor chemistry.
The optimal thermal-ramp threshold depends on composition or synthesis environment.
